hypothesis: Y040 showed triple resets erase all cache benefit. Test whether protecting 3 or 6 of at most 9 existing inactive cached assignments through each reset partially preserves placement capability without increasing simultaneous memory.
environment: Exact Y037 nonaliased 7-active/16-motif, 16-cell circular-radius2 graph, four-way collision, eight episodes per seed; four drift regimes drift1/drift2/drift4/late_shock.
interruption: At starts of episodes 2,4,6 clear previous-active and previous-allocation runtime state. Keep last N cached inactive assignments, with N frozen to 0,3,6,9; no parallel snapshot or second cache; total bounded cache remains <=9.
policies: matched sham with exact same storage and reset actions but no cache reads
legal retained-cache preferences with same cap9 and same reset events
metrics: Per preserve-level×regime (16 cells), every heldout-seed returning-key churn, legal cache preferences, search calls, writes and occupancy. Independent Hall=7 for every episode, equality of cache key/write trajectory across policies.
classification: PROTECTED_MEMORY_BENEFIT if preserve3 saves churn versus preserve0 in at least3/4 regimes and preserve6 improves over preserve3 in at least2/4; PARTIAL if either preserve3 or preserve6 improves over preserve0 in any regime but strict not met; NO_BENEFIT otherwise. Also report baseline preserve9 and adverse outcomes.
controls: Preserve only actually observed pre-interruption cached entries; no future labels or oracle to decision
All arm memory<=9 plus seven active, 16 motifs and cells unchanged; reset scheduling frozen
Exact SHA source/prereg, first-use archived artifact, one complete pytest regression, no retries or accepted-ref changes
claim_limit: Synthetic protected assignment cache after interruptions, not biological or learned semantic repair.
